Summary

Last week declined only 0.37% from its open to its close. See what prices to follow for the start of next week.

S&P 500 futures test whether the channel breakout can hold

S&P 500 E-mini futures have improved after breaking out of the broader descending channel that contained much of the August-to-September pullback. But the four-hour chart is now at the more interesting stage: not whether price can briefly rise above resistance, but whether buyers can keep it there.

After reaching7,848.50 on September 22, ES pulled back through a sequence of lower highs and eventually fell to apx7,672 on October 1. The rebound from that low has been sharp. Price reached7,810.25 on October 2before finishing the latest four-hour bar at7,776.50.

That puts ES around the shorter descending trendline drawn from the September high. The move above it is encouraging, but still looks more like anearly breakout attempt than a completed breakout. The rejection from 7,810 is important because it shows that sellers are still responding above the trendline.

Momentum has improved alongside the recovery. MACD has crossed back above its signal line and moved above zero, while the additional trend evidence in the supplied data has also shifted upward. Volume during the earlier part of the October 2 advance was relatively strong compared with similar time periods, although follow-through later in the session was less impressive. Volatility has also expanded, with the four-hour average trading range rising from the high-20s toward roughly35 points. In a wider-range environment, brief moves through resistance are easier to produce, making follow-through more valuable than the initial break itself.

The first test is therefore roughly7,780-7,810. Sustained four-hour closes above that area, preferably followed by a pullback that holds, would improve the case for another challenge of7,840-7,850. Falling back beneath the breakout area and struggling to recover it would instead reopen7,720-7,740, with the October low near7,673the more important structural reference below.

For readers skeptical of technical analysis, this is a useful example of what charts can and cannot do. A trendline does not predict where ES must go. It creates a testable question about buyer and seller behavior. The informative part is whether price breaks a widely visible boundary, attracts follow-through and then survives the next test of that boundary.

YTD performance of the major stock indices shows where the strength is

The year-to-date comparison highlights a clear growth and technology tilt. TheNasdaq 100 leads with a 22.01% gain, followed by theNasdaq Composite at 16.99%and theS&P 500 at 12.81%. TheDow Jones trails at 6.48%.

Takeaway:The S&P 500 has delivered a solid year, but the stronger performance in the Nasdaq indices suggests that market leadership remains concentrated in growth-heavy areas. For ES traders, that makes continued participation from technology stocks an important confirmation to watch if the S&P 500 breakout is to hold.

What else? I'm also monitoring Intel right now, as the stock's failed rebound below the previous quarter's value-area high leaves buyers searching for stability. With INTC closing at $119.33, I need to see ifnearby support at the $117 to $118 zone can halt further technical deteriorationamid its recent divergence from the broader tech sector.

That broader tech strength is heavily tied to Friday's subdued payroll data. As Greg Michalowski at investingLive.com pointed out,the weak 29,000 jobs print initially sparked a relief rally across US equitiesby easing fears of an October Fed hike.

However, Greg also flagged a critical structural reversal later in the session, noting thatTreasury yields quickly erased their post-report plunge to finish higher, keeping the pressure on European indices despite a modest Friday bounce.

These shifting rate expectations are clearly defining the commodities space as well. According to Giuseppe Dellamotta's latest chart breakdown,gold is finding solid structural footing above the 4,140 level, bolstered by dovish Fed commentary that sharply limits the likelihood of near-term tightening. Meanwhile, currency markets are flashing their own warning signs.

Over on the FX desk, Adam Button highlighted asudden and anomalous plunge in USD/JPY to the daily lows, suggesting potential stealth intervention or a fat-finger event as bond market volatility spills over into major pairs. And what aboutinflation?You can read which one is more important.
